Folks — forwarding Liam's note. He booked through our Calendly link and his Outlook shows 03:00 AM local. Looks like Calendly is passing organizer timezone without a VTIMEZONE block that Outlook/Dublin interprets as UTC.

Short analysis / proposed options:
- Quick fix: generate a manual .ics with an explicit VTIMEZONE for Europe/Dublin and send to Liam (attachment: demo-ics-with-vtimezone.ics). That should pin the time to Aug 30 16:00 BST.
- Platform fix (longer): change Calendly/Chili Piper integration to include TZ identifier (Europe/Dublin) in the single-event .ics and force the TZ parameter in the DTSTART/DTEND lines. Some schedulers only include numeric offsets which break during DST transitions.
- User workaround: ask the customer to select the slot while explicitly verifying the timezone dropdown in Calendly (not great UX).

Rafael: can you produce the ICS with a VTIMEZONE block and include both DST rules (so Outlook picks BST)? Priyom: add a short KB note to the internal scheduling runbook for EU customers explaining the DST edge case.

Thanks — I'll offer the manual invite and a backup slot.

— Olga

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 23 Aug 2029 10:22:07 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Demo slot — quick timezone check before we lock it

Thanks for the heads up. I'm attaching a generated .ics that explicitly sets the timezone to Europe/Dublin (includes VTIMEZONE with BST rules). Should render correctly in Outlook, Apple Calendar, and Google Calendar.

I tested a copy in Outlook desktop (Win11) and it shows Aug 30, 16:00 BST. Notes: Calendly's default export sometimes writes DTSTART:20290830T160000Z (Z suffix) which forces UTC in some clients — that appears to be the root cause here. The ICS I'm attaching uses DTSTART;TZID=Europe/Dublin:20290830T160000 and includes a VTIMEZONE section.

Attachment: demo-ics-with-vtimezone.ics (ICS — pins to Europe/Dublin)

Olga — once you confirm I'll send to Liam with a short note and hold the slot until he confirms. Priyom — can you add the KB snippet: "If customer is in EU/APAC, send ICS with TZ identifier; do not rely on numeric offset only during DST weeks".

Cheers,
Rafael Mendes
Solution Architect | Redwood Inference
